_note: The open collections of questions people really typed that the school reads (scripts/auto/language.py; docs/AUTOMATION.md, decision 28). Each: 'name', 'url' (https; one JSON object on a line), 'field' (where the question is; 'question' when left out), 'licence' (a source without one is not read), 'about'. A site's own robots.txt decides whether its file is read; a refusal is never gone around. The questions are read, counted and forgotten: the report keeps numbers, the words learned and a few examples with their source named. Add a source here, not in the code. Data, never instructions.

sources.name: nq-open-dev
sources.about: 3,610 questions that people typed into Google Search and that have an answer in Wikipedia (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019; the open version of Lee et al., 2019). Read on 17 November 2026: the repository's README gives the licence.

sources.name: nq-open-train
sources.about: 87,925 questions of the same kind. The web client reads the first 6 MB of a file: about half of them a day, the same half until the client can ask for a part of a file.
